issue.title: CI 3.12 coverage leg hit ~850 sase_core_rs import NameErrors mid-run
issue.description:
GitHub Actions run 31070896895 (master commit 3e4b5955c), job 'test (3.12)' / 'Run tests (coverage leg)', failed ~850 tests with the same error raised from the installed extension package itself:

  .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sase_core_rs/__init__.py:3: NameError
      from .sase_core_rs import *
  >   __doc__ = sase_core_rs.__doc__
  E   NameError: name 'sase_core_rs' is not defined

That is maturin's generated mixed-layout __init__.py, so the native submodule import left the package name unbound. Downstream assertions show the breakage leaking into user-visible strings, e.g. "report could not be loaded: name 'sase_core_rs' is not defined" where the test expected 'plans unavailable'.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the storm buries the real signal. That run's genuinely actionable failure was one node (the artifact-ref commit parity test); a reader scanning 850+ FAILED lines cannot see it. It is also the only observed case of the prebuilt wheel failing to import after the setup step reported '[setup] Installing prebuilt sase_core_rs wheel ... 0.18.2 ... whl' successfully.

SCOPE: reproduce or explain the unbound-submodule failure, then make it fail loudly and once instead of 850 times - for example an import smoke check in the coverage leg between install and pytest, or a session-start guard that aborts the run when sase_core_rs is unimportable.

EVIDENCE / FREQUENCY: seen once so far, only on the 3.12 coverage leg. The 3.13 and 3.14 legs of the same run, and the 3.12 leg of the adjacent runs 31070151356 and 31067580370, did not show it. Plausible leads worth checking first: a race between 'uv pip install' rewriting site-packages and the already-running pytest workers (the coverage leg is the only leg that runs 'just test-cov', and the setup step reinstalls 9 packages immediately before pytest starts), or per-worker import of a partially-written .so.

Found on 2026-08-06 while diagnosing the master CI failure; unrelated to that fix, which only touches tests/_run_pytest_fixtures.py and the tools/run_pytest test modules.

evidence.note:
Second occurrence, independently verified from the job log while landing epic sase-fq.8. Master CI run 31114984919 (sha 7cbfc3449), job 'test (3.12)' / 'Run tests (coverage leg)': 27 failed, 25967 passed in 1477s; 26 of the 27 are "NameError: name 'sase_core_rs' is not defined" raised from .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sase_core_rs/__init__.py:3 (grep counts 52 occurrences across the log, i.e. the traceback plus the FAILED summary line for each), plus one downstream 'assert False is True' in tests/ace/tui/test_notification_custom_gate.py::test_tracked_executor_reports_terminal_and_extra_commands_live. Affected modules cluster in the sase_core binding tests: tests/test_core_notification_store.py, tests/test_core_status_lines.py, tests/test_core_vcs_log.py.

WHAT THIS ADDS BEYOND THE ORIGINAL REPORT: (1) The wheel version is not the variable. The original occurrence (run 31070896895) ran sase_core_rs 0.18.2; this one ran 0.18.4 -- 'Install dependencies' logged '+ sase-core-rs==0.18.4 (from file:///home/runner/work/_temp/sase-core-wheel/sase_core_rs-0.18.4-cp312-abi3-manylinux_2_39_x86_64.whl)' and the run step re-exported the same SASE_CORE_WHEEL. So the unbound-submodule failure is not specific to one build. (2) Still only the 3.12 coverage leg. The 3.13 leg of the same run had exactly 1 failure (an unrelated ACE title flake) and 3.14 had 0, both on wheels installed by the same setup path. That keeps the 'coverage leg reinstalls site-packages immediately before pytest starts' lead as the strongest one in the bead's SCOPE section. (3) The blast-radius argument holds: the epic that was landing needed to read this run's failure summary to confirm its own parity test, and 26 NameErrors is what a reader has to scan past first.

NOT caused by epic sase-fq/sase-fq.8: that epic's fix is a pytest env-isolation fix in tests/_run_pytest_fixtures.py and tests/_tmp_leak_guard.py, which cannot affect whether the installed extension package binds its native submodule, and the failure predates it (run 31070896895, 2026-08-06 01:40).

payload.entry:
RESOLVED BY EPIC sase-gg (land verification, 2026-08-06): this bead's SCOPE — 'reproduce or explain the unbound-submodule failure' — is now answered, and the defect is fixed on both sides.

ROOT CAUSE (not a race, not a partially-written .so): maturin's generated sase_core_rs/__init__.py reads a bare 'sase_core_rs' on line 3 that the file never binds. It resolves only because importlib's CACHE-MISS path does setattr(parent_package, child_name, child_module) into what happens to be that file's global namespace. Evict or swap the PARENT package from sys.modules while the compiled submodule sase_core_rs.sase_core_rs stays cached, and the next import returns the submodule from cache, skips that setattr, and raises NameError — poisoning every later import in the process. Under pytest-xdist that means every later test scheduled onto that worker, which is why the count varied (850 vs 27) and why only some legs saw it: xdist assigns tests to workers dynamically, so WHICH tests share the poisoned process changes run to run. Reproduced deterministically against the published wheel with: import sase_core_rs; del sys.modules['sase_core_rs']; importlib.import_module('sase_core_rs').

The window was opened by 14 test modules that patched sys.modules[RUST_EXTENSION_MODULE_NAME] parent-only via monkeypatch.setitem/delitem.

FIXES LANDED: (1) sase commit 08f1b28f8 adds tests/_rust_extension_module_helpers.py, which moves the compiled submodule with its parent under monkeypatch so teardown restores both together, routes all 14 patch sites through it, and pins the invariant in tests/test_rust_extension_module_helpers.py. (2) sase-core PR #89 (https://github.com/sase-org/sase-core/pull/89) ships an explicit python/sase_core_rs/__init__.py that binds the submodule by name, fixing the root cause for every consumer; that PR is OPEN and awaiting the owner's merge/publish decision.

EVIDENCE THE STORM IS GONE: master CI run 31123018619 (commit baebfcd21, first complete run after the epic landed) has test (3.12), test (3.14) and coverage-contexts all green. Locally the 14 patched modules plus the new helper tests pass 271/271 both serially and under -n 4 xdist splits.

STILL OPEN FROM THIS BEAD'S SCOPE: the 'fail loudly and once instead of 850 times' half — an import smoke check between install and pytest, or a session-start guard. The epic removed the cause but added no such guard, so a future import breakage would still storm. Recommend the owner either close this as done on the root-cause fix or narrow it to that guard.
